note:
ROUND 3 of the medical explainer set for /pages/copper-peptide-research, blocks f1, f2, f3. Malcolm supplied four new reference images and asked for the mechanism to be understood FIRST and the styling matched second.

WHAT EACH BLOCK HAS TO EXPLAIN — stated before the briefs, because rounds 1 and 2 were styled without this being written down and drifted into decoration:
  f1  Pickart & Margolina 2018: GHK-Cu supports the skin's own collagen, elastin and glycosaminoglycan production. The active must reach the DERMIS, where the fibre network lives, and that network must be visibly denser and brighter where it arrives.
  f2  Kang 2009: increased activity of skin-renewal cells (keratinocytes) and basal-cell markers, in cultured cells and skin-equivalent models. The active must reach the BASAL LAYER — the bottom row of the epidermis — and those cells must plump, brighten and divide. It is a LAB MODEL, so an isolated specimen block, never a body.
  f3  Miller 2006: users reported greater SATISFACTION with appearance over 12 weeks. Self-reported, not a measured change. So f3 shows topical arrival and absorption at the surface and nothing more — no densifying, no plumping comparison, no split.

WHY ROUNDS 1 AND 2 MISSED, and it is not the activation dynamic — round 2 fixed that. It is that they were not recognisably SKIN. Rounds 1-2 built an abstract world of white pebbles and hourglass columns on a pale ground: elegant, but it reads as a material study. Every one of Malcolm's four references is a CROSS-SECTION OF SKIN with three legible strata — a textured surface layer on top, a stack of rounded cells beneath it, and a deeper zone of long wavy fibre bundles running horizontally. The viewer is meant to recognise the place before they read the event.

FOUR DEVICES TAKEN FROM THE REFERENCES:
  1. LAYERED CROSS-SECTION. Surface, cell stack, fibre zone — all three visible in one frame.
  2. ACTIVES AS TRANSLUCENT SPHERES held above the surface, each containing a small cluster of beads.
  3. EXPLICIT DOWNWARD DELIVERY. Reference 2 fires a shaft of light from each sphere down through the surface; reference 4 uses white curved arrows. SHAFTS ARE USED HERE, NOT ARROWS: an arrow is a graphic overlay that these engines render crudely, and a light shaft carries the same direction as a physical event. Arrows stay negated.
  4. STARBURST GLINTS at the point of arrival — small bright star-shaped sparkles, the genre's signature for 'this is where it acts'.

A NEGATIVE FROM ROUND 2 HAD TO BE REMOVED, and this is the trap worth recording. Round 2 negated 'no sparks, no fireworks, no starburst' to keep the glow from going electrical. Malcolm's references use starburst sparkle as the central arrival cue, so that negative now fights the brief. It is gone; only the genuinely electrical terms are still barred — lightning, electric arc, laser, neon. A negative list has to be re-read against every new brief, not inherited.

COLOUR — THE REFERENCES RESOLVE THE CONFLICT RAISED IN ROUND 2. All four are pink, and round 2 argued against pink because blush is PDRN's scene colour. The references are pink because SKIN is pink: that is anatomy, not a brand assignment. And reference 4 shows the way through — warm skin with BLUE-LILAC collagen fibres. So the tissue here is a soft desaturated peach-cream, warm enough to read as skin but held well back from PDRN's saturated blush; the fibre network is Clinical blue 014EB1; and the active is a blue sphere with copper B87333 beads inside. Brand identity sits on the two things that are ours — the active and the collagen — while the tissue is simply tissue.

Square 2048x2048, measured off the live DOM. CLASS B, no references attached, FLUX.2 in the run. Rounds 1 and 2 are KEPT and remain pickable.

slots.title: f1 · delivery into the dermis, the fibre network densifying where it lands
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

A block of skin is shown in cross-section, seen from a low three-quarter angle so both its top surface and its cut face are visible, occupying the lower two thirds of the frame. Three strata are clearly legible from top to bottom: a thin outer layer with a fine irregular texture of soft interlocking plates; beneath it a stack of two or three rows of flattened rounded translucent cells packed neatly together; and below that an open deeper zone filled with long wavy bundles of glossy fibre running horizontally through it, curving and overlapping in loose parallel waves. The tissue is a soft desaturated peach-cream, warm and pale. The fibre bundles are a clear vivid blue, colour hex 014EB1, glassy and translucent, standing out distinctly against the warm tissue around them.

Above the surface, floating in the hazy air, are three translucent spheres of clear pale blue, each holding a small cluster of polished copper beads, colour hex B87333, suspended inside. From the underside of each sphere a slender shaft of warm white light descends straight down, piercing the outer layer and passing through the cell rows into the deep fibre zone below.

WHERE EACH SHAFT REACHES THE FIBRES, a bright star-shaped glint bursts and a warm bloom spreads outward through the bundles. Around those points the fibres are markedly thicker, denser, more numerous and lit from within, several fine new strands weaving between the older ones; further from any shaft the bundles are sparser, thinner and duller, and the change between the two is smooth and gradual across the frame. Small bright sparkles drift in the lit zones.

Soft diffuse light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field, the far edge of the block dissolving into pale haze. Glossy, luminous, immaculate.

slots.title: f2 · laboratory skin model, the active reaching the basal row
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

A small rectangular block of laboratory-grown skin tissue is shown in cross-section, seen from a low three-quarter angle, isolated in clean empty space with nothing around it so it reads unmistakably as a specimen rather than part of a body. Its cut face fills the middle of the frame. From top to bottom: a thin outer layer with a fine irregular surface texture; then many stacked rows of rounded translucent cells, broad and flattened in the upper rows and becoming rounder further down; and at the very bottom of the stack a single distinct row of noticeably plumper, taller, column-shaped cells sitting on a smooth translucent base. The tissue is a soft desaturated peach-cream, warm and pale.

Above the block float three translucent spheres of clear pale blue, each holding a small cluster of polished copper beads, colour hex B87333. From the underside of each, a slender shaft of warm white light descends, piercing the outer layer and travelling down through every row to reach the bottom row.

THE BOTTOM ROW IS WHERE EVERYTHING HAPPENS. Where each shaft arrives, a bright star-shaped glint bursts against those plump base cells and a warm bloom spreads along the row. The base cells nearest a shaft are markedly rounder, fuller and brighter than any other cell in the block, their membranes crisp and lit from within, and two of them are pinched into a figure-of-eight in the act of becoming two. Along the row, cells further from a shaft are progressively flatter and duller. From the lit base cells a soft glow rises upward through the rows above, weakening as it climbs, so the upper rows are only faintly warmed. Small bright sparkles drift near the lit zone.

Soft diffuse light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field, the block's far edge dissolving into pale haze. Glossy, luminous, immaculate.

slots.title: f3 · topical arrival and absorption at the surface
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

The outer surface of skin fills the lower half of the frame, seen from a low raking angle so it recedes into the distance. It is a fine, even, regular relief of soft interlocking plates divided by shallow channels, smooth and refined, with the rounded shapes of the cells just beneath showing faintly through its translucency. The tissue is a soft desaturated peach-cream, warm and pale, with a delicate glossy sheen along the raised edges.

Four translucent spheres of clear pale blue hover just above the surface at different heights, each holding a small cluster of polished copper beads, colour hex B87333, suspended inside. The nearest and largest sphere is in contact with the surface: its underside is flattened and beginning to sink in, and a soft ring-shaped ripple spreads outward across the surface from the point where it meets. At that contact a bright star-shaped glint bursts and a warm bloom glows up through the translucent surface from just underneath, spreading a short way outward beneath the plates and fading. A second, smaller sphere further off has already half-sunk, only its dome still showing.

From the two spheres still in the air, slender shafts of warm white light reach down toward the surface. Small bright sparkles and a scatter of tiny clear droplets drift through the air around them.

The upper half of the frame is soft empty pale gradient, luminous and clean. Soft diffuse light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field. Glossy, luminous, immaculate.
